notesStmt.note: The corrections on this proof were likely made in late 1889, shortly before the poem's publication in December.

A corrected proof slip of a poem that was published under the title "A Christmas Greeting." Whitman told his associate Horace Traubel on December 9, 1889, that the poem had been accepted for publication by the McClure newspaper syndicate (after initially being rejected by Harper's) and that he suspected it would be published around Christmas. The poem appeared in the St. Louis Post-Dispatch on December 22, 1889, with a note indicating that it was "written for the Sunday Post-Dispatch." It is possible that it also appeared in other papers around that time. Whitman, however, was unaware of its publication, wondering as late as January 29, 1890, why it had not appeared in the U.S., despite having appeared by that time in a Parisian newspaper. The poem was later included in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891).

lg.head: A CHRISTMAS GREETING

head.hi: From a Northern Star-Group to a Southern.

lg.l: Welcome, Brazilian brother—thy ample place is ready;

A loving hand—a smile from the north—a sunny instant
hail!

(Let the future care for itself, where it reveals its troubles,
impedimentas,

Ours, ours the present throe, the democratic aim, the accept-
anceacceptance
and the faith;)

To thee to-day, our reaching arm, our turning neck—to thee
from us the expectant eye,

Thou cluster free! thou brilliant lustrous star! thou, learning
well,
The true lesson of a nation's light in the sky,
(More shining than the Cross, more than the Crown,)
The height to be superb humanity.
